Charities such as Stepping Stones China, Shanghai Sunrise, Heart to Heart Shanghai and Shanghai Young Bakers take expat volunteers for teaching, fundraising and events.
venue: Stepping Stones China / Shanghai Sunrise (SmartShanghai list)

how: Many studios such as Body & Soul Yoga Club, Pure Yoga (IAPM Mall) and Hatha Yoga Boutique run beginner-to-advanced classes in English and Chinese.
No cliffs or tall natural exposures in the flat delta and BASE jumping from buildings is illegal; nearest sites are Zhangjiajie or Tianmen Mountain in Hunan, a 2-hour flight away.
No bullfighting tradition and not practised legally in China; the nearest are in Spain or Portugal, a 12 hour flight.
Long Beach Tower in Baoshan has a bungee-style vertical free-fall jump from platforms 12-19 m high inside a vertical adventure park; no open-air bungee site found.
venue: Long Beach Tower vertical adventure park

how: Flat delta terrain has no gorges or canyons; the nearest canyoning is in the Zhejiang and Anhui mountains, roughly 3-4 hours away.
Delta alluvial plain has no limestone caves or flooded cave systems; the nearest cave systems are in the Zhejiang and Anhui karst areas, 3-4 hours away, and recreational cave diving is rare in China.
Shanghai sits on a flat Yangtze delta plain with no karst or natural caves; the nearest show caves and wild caving are in Yixing (Jiangsu) and Hangzhou-area Zhejiang, roughly 2-3 hours away.
Climate with only about 5 snowy days a year rules out snow dog sledding; the nearest is in Heilongjiang or Jilin, a 2.5-3 hour flight north.
No glaciers in the flat Yangtze delta; the nearest glaciers are in western China (Yulong Snow Mountain, Yunnan, or Tibet), a 3-4 hour flight away.
A sports centre named Magic Jungle (Mo Du Ju Zhen) near Lujiazui is tagged as a climbing-adventure facility in OpenStreetMap; the exact format (ropes or indoor adventure) is not confirmed.
UFLY Skydiving Club ran a cylindrical vertical wind tunnel with two-minute sessions (2014 report); simulated freefall and current operation unconfirmed.
L*SNOW Indoor Skiing Theme Resort in Pudong's Nanhui area (Dishui Lake) is a very large indoor ski and snow resort, roughly 55-60 km southeast of the centre.

The only luge track in China is the Yanqing National Sliding Centre near Beijing, roughly 1,000 km away (about 2.5 hours by flight or 5 hours by high-speed rail plus transfer); Shanghai has no sliding track.

Flat Yangtze delta (average about 4 m above sea level, highest hill Sheshan 118 m) has no mountains; nearest real mountaineering is Huangshan or Mount Tianmu in Anhui/Zhejiang, roughly 3-5 hours away by high-speed rail and road.
Shanghai has no hills or slopes for flying; the nearest paragliding training base is Yangzishan in Zhejiang (tandem flights advertised around 680 CNY in 2019), about 3 hours away.
No ranching or rodeo culture in the Shanghai metro area; bull riding and horse sports are found in Inner Mongolia and Xinjiang, a long flight away.
Shanghai Wild Animal Park in Pudong has a vehicle-entry drive-through zone among free-roaming animals plus walk-through areas; it is a safari-style park, not wild safari.
No desert in the metro area; nearest desert dunes are in Inner Mongolia or Gansu, a 3-4 hour flight west.
Ski and snowboard simulators are in malls across the city, e.g. Rossignol Mountain Sports Academy at Taikoo Hui; over 100 simulators reported citywide.
Natural snow is rare (about 5 days a year) and there are no mountains; nearest natural-snow skiing is in Zhejiang/Anhui winter resorts or Jilin, about 3 hours by flight.
No volcanoes anywhere near the delta; nearest is Changbai Mountain in Jilin or Tianchi areas, a 3 hour flight north.
Flat delta with slow tidal rivers has no whitewater; nearest river rafting is in Zhejiang (for example Fuchunjiang or Anji area) around 2-3 hours away.
